_help: Fallback for banks centralbank.watch does not publish probabilities for (it links out to CME FedWatch for the Fed, and omits the RBNZ). Fill hike/hold/cut as percentages plus next_meeting and src. Set "override": true to beat a scraped value. Leave a bank out entirely rather than guessing - a missing expectation is handled, an invented one is not.
_note_USD: 16 Sep FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% (confirmed) with a hawkish dot plot (16 of 18 officials expect at least one more hike this year). That meeting has now passed, so the prior entry (which pointed at it) is stale - decision-day trap. No credible market-implied probability for the next meeting (28 Oct) was found: WebSearch turned up only the qualitative dot-plot signal, and the internal Fed Watch model (data/fedwatch.json) is currently broken post-hike (still using the pre-hike EFFR/target range as of 15 Sep, producing a nonsensical Dec reading). Left out entirely rather than guessing - re-research once a clean Oct 28 figure is available.

JPY.src: researched 2026-09-23. Decision-day trap: the prior entry pointed at the 18 Sep meeting, which has now happened (BOJ hiked 25bp to 1.25%, 7-2 vote, fastest hike-to-hike gap of the cycle - see speech_tone.json JPY BOJ entries). Confirmed via boj.or.jp official schedule that the next Monetary Policy Meeting is 29-30 Oct 2026 (decision due 30 Oct). Market pricing has swung to a pause after the September move - public reporting puts the October hike probability at roughly 22% (78% hold), consistent with 'not back-to-back' commentary. centralbank.watch's own BoJ page gave inconsistent/self-contradictory output when queried directly (mixed up meeting dates), so not used as the source here; override true.

EUR.src: researched 2026-09-27 (refresh of the 10 Sep entry). Futures pricing on 24 Sep implied ~60% for a 25bp hike to 2.75% on 29 Oct (Admiral Markets citing ECB Watch), up from ~29% after the 10 Sep hike. Other snapshots range 47-75% depending on day/source, so the 24 Sep ECB Watch figure is used as the mid. Lagarde 18 Sep leaned against automatic tightening; pricing moves daily.

NZD.src: researched 2026-09-27 (refresh of the 10 Sep entry). Money markets price ~75% for a 25bp OCR hike to 3.00% on 28 Oct, up from ~57% after Governor Breman said on 22 Sep that persistent higher oil would push near-term inflation above the September MPS (Pound Sterling Live, 22 Sep; FXStreet). centralbank.watch's older ~88% hold snapshot is stale.

CAD.src: researched 2026-09-27 (refresh of the 10 Sep entry). As of 25 Sep, OIS pricing implied a 59% probability of a BoC hike on 28 Oct (+15bp implied from 2.25%), per money.ca/refdesk; odds were ~6% hold-dominant before 2 Sep and jumped on oil, bond yields and the Fed's 16 Sep hike. Several bank economists still expect a hold until Q1 2027.

_note_CAD: Rate-odds source rotated to public reporting after bankofcanadaodds.com; the TradingView scrape carries a stale 5.25% BoC rate and no real BoC block, so override stays true. If a cleaner current feed appears, prefer it.
